strengths: Strong empirical motivation with compelling analysis of scale and spatial redundancy in VAR (Figures 2-3)
Substantial practical efficiency gains: 3.0-4.2× GPU memory reduction without sacrificing performance
Comprehensive experimental validation including thorough ablation studies and comparisons across multiple baseline categories
Technically sound implementation with clear mathematical formulation and good presentation
Competitive or superior quantitative results (FID 3.09 vs 3.55 for VAR-310M; IS 285.5 vs 280.4)
weaknesses: Limited novelty: scale-Markov conditioning and spatial-Markov attention are straightforward applications of existing concepts (local window attention is well-established)

Weak theoretical justification for Markovian assumptions: no principled analysis of approximation error or formal characterization of information loss from discarding non-adjacent scales
Fine-tuning results conflate multiple factors: unclear whether improvements come from Markovian conditioning, fine-tuning itself, or different computational allocation

strengths: Clear empirical motivation: Figures 2-3 convincingly demonstrate that attention in VAR concentrates on adjacent scales and local spatial regions, providing good justification for the proposed constraints
Significant practical efficiency improvements: 2.6-3.2× memory reduction during training/inference and elimination of KV cache requirements provide real value for practitioners

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Tests across diverse baselines (GANs, diffusion, token-wise AR, scale-wise AR), both small trained-from-scratch and larger fine-tuned models, with ablation studies
Generally well-written presentation: Clear explanations and effective visualizations (Figures 1-4) that communicate the core concepts effectively
Good reproducibility support: Detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, and training settings provided in appendices
weaknesses: Limited novelty: The core contributions are straightforward applications of known techniques—conditional independence assumptions and neighborhood attention ([13], [14])—to VAR. No fundamentally new modeling insights or algorithms are introduced

Misleading 'Markovian' terminology: Equation (4) simply conditions on an adjacent scale (conditional independence), not a true Markov process. No formal justification is provided for why omitting non-adjacent scales is valid; empirical attention concentration doesn't prove information redundancy. 'Spatial-Markov attention' conflates standard local attention with Markovian properties

Modest performance improvements: FID improves 0.46 points (3.55→3.09), IS improves 5.1 points (280.4→285.5), Precision/Recall marginally change. No error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs reported make it unclear if differences are statistically significant for claims of 'superior performance'

Inconsistent experimental methodology: Table 1 trains 310M from scratch but larger models (600M, 1B) only report fine-tuning in Table 2. This makes MVAR† results not directly comparable to VAR baselines. Different batch sizes across model sizes (Table 5) and ablations on 50-epoch schedules vs. 300-epoch main training complicate fair comparison

Contradictory ablation findings: Table 3 shows conditioning on only 1 scale (method d: FID=4.35) outperforms conditioning on 3 scales (method c: FID=4.86), directly contradicting the main approach. The paper doesn't adequately explain this counterintuitive result or clarify its relationship to reported main results

Limited evaluation scope: Only ImageNet 256×256 tested; no higher resolution experiments where efficiency gains matter more. Single-dataset evaluation raises generalization questions. No analysis of per-operation wall-clock speedup (Table 2 times are ambiguous), no downstream task evaluation or human studies

Incomplete technical justification: Paper shows attention is concentrated locally but doesn't deeply explain why or whether this is architecture/dataset-specific or fundamental. No analysis of constant factors in O(Nk) complexity; with k=49, practical speedups depend on implementation details not discussed. The relationship between parallel training with diagonal masks (Appendix A) and scale-Markov assumption (Eq. 4) conflates training procedure with model formulation

Missing critical comparisons: No comparison to concurrent efficient VAR variants or other local attention mechanisms in AR. Reproducibility claim incomplete: abstract states 'Codes and models:' with no actual URL provided

Statistical rigor concerns: No error bars, confidence intervals, or results from multiple runs despite modest performance improvements. For a top-tier venue, this is insufficient support for claims of performance superiority

Overclaiming and framing issues: Abstract claims 'comparable or superior performance' when improvements are marginal and potentially within noise. The distinction between core algorithmic novelty vs. engineering choices is insufficiently clear

strengths: Well-motivated empirical analysis: Figures 2-3 convincingly demonstrate scale and spatial redundancy in VAR through attention weight visualizations and attention maps
Significant practical impact: 3-4× memory reduction (4.2× at inference) and complete elimination of KV cache, enabling training on modest hardware (8 RTX 4090 GPUs)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple model sizes (310M-1B), detailed ablations on key components, multiple metrics, and pre-trained/fine-tuning comparisons showing consistent improvements
Strong computational complexity reduction: From O(N²) to O(N·k) with clear mathematical derivation and detailed complexity analysis in appendix
Technically sound methodology: Clean mathematical formulation (Eqs. 4-7), clever diagonal causal mask strategy for parallel training, and thorough implementation documentation
Thorough ablation studies: Systematic analysis of conditioning prefix length, neighborhood size k, and ablations on individual components with clear progression
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-structured paper with effective visualizations, detailed hyperparameters (Table 5), and good implementation details
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Markovian assumptions and neighborhood attention are well-established techniques; the contribution is primarily engineering-focused optimization of VAR rather than introducing new modeling principles

Weak theoretical justification for scale-Markovian assumption: Attention weight distributions do not rigorously prove conditional independence; information could still flow through other mechanisms even with low attention weights, and no analysis of actual modeling capacity loss
Modest performance improvements: FID gains are marginal (3.09 vs 3.55 on 310M, 2.23 vs 2.33 on 1B), with larger models showing negligible improvements; no statistical significance testing provided

Asymmetric and unjustified training procedure: Scales r9-r10 (60% of tokens) revert to single-scale conditioning without causal masking, contradicting the claimed uniform scale-Markovian approach; this design choice lacks explanation

Limited experimental scope: Only ImageNet 256×256 evaluated; no higher-resolution experiments where efficiency matters most; only class-conditional generation tested; missing comparisons with concurrent efficiency methods (HART, FastVAR, collaborative decoding)

Fixed hyperparameter choices lack generalization analysis: k=7×7 neighborhood chosen empirically but not validated to generalize across resolutions or other domains; k is relatively large (49 tokens) limiting complexity savings

Incomplete analysis of discrepancies: Table 2 shows decreased Recall in some cases; Table 3 shows non-linear scaling behavior with single-scale conditioning (FID 4.35 on 310M vs 2.23 on 1B) that isn't explained
Unanswered generalization questions: No evidence that Markovian assumptions hold for higher resolutions, text-to-image synthesis, or other conditioning modalities; limited to single benchmark

strengths: Well-motivated empirical observations: Figures 2-3 convincingly demonstrate scale and spatial redundancy in vanilla next-scale prediction through attention weight analysis
Significant practical improvements: 3-4× memory reduction during both training and inference, enabling training on 8 RTX 4090 GPUs instead of requiring substantially larger resources
Comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple datasets (ImageNet, CelebA, FFHQ), resolutions (256×512), model sizes (310M-2B), with thorough ablations examining each component's contribution
Clear presentation and visualization: Figures effectively communicate conceptual differences; paper is well-written and easy to follow
Solid empirical results: MVAR achieves comparable or superior generation quality (e.g., FID 3.09 vs 3.55 for VAR-d16) while substantially reducing memory footprint
Good reproducibility: Detailed implementation details, hyperparameter settings in appendices, commitment to release code
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Scale-Markov conditioning is a straightforward simplification rather than a novel principle; spatial-Markov attention is well-established (Hassani & Shi 2022) with main contribution being application to VAR rather than methodological advance

Insufficient justification of Markovian assumptions: Attention weight analysis shows concentration on adjacent structures but doesn't prove information from non-adjacent scales is unnecessary; no quantitative analysis of information loss; improvements could stem from regularization rather than removing true redundancy

Marginal quality improvements lack statistical rigor: FID improvements range from 0.08-0.46 depending on model; IS improvements 1-5%; no statistical significance testing or error bars; improvements could be within noise margins

Unfair experimental comparisons: Section D.1 acknowledges inability to replicate original VAR settings; Table 2 uses different batch sizes and schedules; VAR-d24 hits OOM making direct comparison impossible; confounding factors obscure whether improvements are from method or implementation

Complex mixed training strategy: Parallel training for r1-r8 with custom CUDA kernels for r9-r10 adds implementation complexity; Figure 9 shows concatenated training also works, questioning necessity of mixed approach

Missing critical ablations and comparisons: No comparison with other VAR efficiency methods (FastVAR mentioned but not compared); no ablation training VAR with identical Markovian constraints to isolate MVAR's unique contribution from regularization effects

Hyperparameter selection lacks principled guidance: Neighborhood size k requires empirical tuning with no theoretical justification; unclear how to select k for new resolutions or domains; Table 9 shows performance is stable but still requires tuning

Limited theoretical analysis and generalization: No formal analysis of approximation quality or information-theoretic bounds; all experiments on resolutions ≤512×512; unclear if assumptions hold at higher resolutions; limited exploration beyond natural images

Insufficient analysis of why removing dependencies improves performance: Paper shows MVAR works but doesn't explain why discarding non-adjacent scale connections sometimes improves over baseline; unclear if information is truly redundant

Modest gains relative to complexity: While memory efficiency is significant, generation quality improvements are small and require complex training procedures, limiting impact for scenarios where memory is not the bottleneck

strengths: Strong empirical motivation with convincing attention weight analysis demonstrating scale and spatial redundancy in VAR
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple model sizes (310M-2B), datasets (ImageNet, CelebA, FFHQ), and resolutions with thorough ablations
Significant practical improvements achieving 3-4× memory reduction and KV cache elimination while maintaining or slightly improving quality
Technically sound implementation with correct complexity analysis (O(N²) → O(Nk)) and well-documented details enabling reproducibility
Clear presentation with effective visualizations that clearly communicate core concepts
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: scale-Markov is straightforward engineering without principled justification; spatial-Markov attention directly applies existing neighborhood attention (Hassani & Shi 2022) without novel mechanisms

Weak theoretical foundation relying solely on empirical attention patterns to infer independence; no first-principles analysis of why conditional independence should hold or its information-theoretic implications

Modest quality improvements (FID improvements of 0.46, 0.08, 0.10 for d16/d20/d24 respectively fall within noise margins) despite substantial memory gains; improvements don't justify fundamental architectural changes
Circular reasoning: using attention weights to justify independence assumptions, then observing expected attention patterns in resulting architecture
Inelegant mixed training strategy with ad-hoc ratio (8:1:1); inconsistencies between training from scratch vs. fine-tuning (Table 2) inadequately explained; added complexity may limit adoption

Limited baseline comparisons: no comparison with other efficient attention mechanisms, sparse attention variants, or other ways to reduce VAR memory; missing ablation isolating spatial-Markov contribution alone
Inference speedup (~20%, Table 2) doesn't match memory reduction (4.2×), suggesting other bottlenecks not analyzed; relationship between FLOPs reduction and wall-clock time unclear
Hyperparameter k chosen empirically (7×7); limited sensitivity analysis across resolutions and model depths despite claims of robustness; Table 9 shows non-negligible variations
Overstatement of novelty through 'Markovian' framing when contributions are essentially engineering optimizations of VAR combining known techniques without new insights into visual generation

strengths: Well-motivated empirical analysis (Figures 2-3) showing attention concentration on adjacent scales and spatial locality, providing clear justification for Markovian assumptions
Significant practical impact: 3.0-3.2× GPU memory reduction enabling training on 8 RTX 4090s instead of expensive A100 setups, with elimination of KV cache during inference

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (ImageNet-256/512, CelebA, FFHQ), model sizes (310M-2B), and thorough ablation studies (Tables 3-4, Figures 7-9) demonstrating consistency
Strong technical execution with rigorous O(N²) to O(Nk) complexity analysis, pragmatic mixed training strategy, and detailed hyperparameters supporting reproducibility
Maintained or improved generation quality (FID: 3.09 vs 3.55, IS: 285.5 vs 280.4) while reducing computational burden, with fine-tuning results showing broad applicability
Clear presentation with well-designed figures illustrating concepts progressively from motivation through method to results
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: scale Markovian assumptions and spatial-Markov attention are straightforward applications of existing techniques (directly borrowed from Hassani & Shi, 2022); main contribution is combining known methods in VAR context, which is somewhat incremental

Empirical observations require careful interpretation—attention concentration on adjacent scales does not necessarily imply other scales are redundant; term 'redundancy' used loosely and claims of 'approximate conditional independence' stronger than figure evidence supports

Experimental setup differences reduce comparison rigor: VAR trained on 256 A100 GPUs with batch size 768 vs MVAR on 8 RTX 4090s; authors acknowledge inability to 'exactly replicate experimental settings'; ImageNet-512 results constrained by resources
Lack of theoretical understanding of why reducing attention scope improves metrics despite reducing expressiveness; missing rigorous analysis of regularization effects vs. information loss

Quality improvements are modest (FID reduction of 0.46, recall decreases in d20), making the main value proposition computational efficiency rather than generation quality—for top-tier venues, this may be considered incremental
Implementation complexity with custom CUDA kernels for scales r9-r10 and architecture-specific mixed training strategy may limit generalizability and adoption compared to simpler methods
Incomplete trade-off analysis: no systematic evaluation of failure cases, generation diversity, or comparisons with other efficiency techniques (KV cache pruning, distillation)
